evidence.snippet: From the recycling side, I see three main issues. First, the incoming loads pile up near the sorting station because we don't have a clear staging area. Second, when we find hazardous items mixed in, there's no standard way to handle them—people improvise. Third, the contamination from unsorted materials slows everything down.

Yes, that's the core of it. If we fix those five things, the line will run much smoother. The staging area and layout redesign will help with throughput, the hazardous waste guide will reduce confusion and risk, and the cleaning routine plus rotation will keep people safer and less fatigued.
And I'll start drafting the hazardous waste guide and the SOP for sorting. I'll have a first version ready by end of week for review.

Good question. A contaminant is anything that reduces the quality or safety of the final material. So yes, a plastic bag in metal is a contaminant because it can jam equipment downstream. I'll add a definition and examples to the SOP.

Batteries and electronics are always hazardous because they contain heavy metals and can leak. I'll make that explicit in the SOP with a visual guide. We'll also have a separate hazardous waste guide that goes into more detail, but the SOP should flag them clearly.
